 This stat might be the best illustration of what makes Derrick White special.
 In Boston's 98-93 win over Toronto on Wednesday, White finished with 19 points while shooting 3-for-7 from 3-point range. He also blocked a game-high four shots despite being the shortest player in Boston's starting lineup.
 As NBC Sports statistician Dick Lipe pointed out , White now has 23 games in which he's made at least three 3-pointers and recorded at least three blocks. That's the eighth-most in NBA history .
 It's even more impressive when you see who the only players with more are:
 Brook Lopez (49)
 Kevin Durant (47)
 Myles Turner (47)
 Kristaps Porzingis (45)
 Victor Wembanyama (39)
 Jaren Jackson Jr. (28)
 Dirk Nowitzki (26)
 Derrick White (23) 
 Rasheed Wallace (22)
 MORE:   NBA Expert Makes Bold Celtics Declaration In Latest Power Rankings 
 White has more games with at least three 3-pointers and three blocks than any other guard in NBA history.
 The only players ahead of him are all at least 6-foot-10.
 Remember, White is only 6-foot-4. Making 3-pointers isn't the hard part for him — he's averaged 2.0 made 3-pointers per game throughout his career — but players his size aren't supposed to protect the rim as effectively as he does.
 White now has 553 blocks in his NBA career. The only guards with more are Dwyane Wade, Michael Jordan, Ron Harper, Clyde Drexler, James Harden, Dennis Johnson and Kobe Bryant.
 It's not often you find a 6-foot-4 guard who can impact a game both as a 3-point shooter and a rim protector. That's what makes White so unique.
